title: The Essentials — PSP's Signature Library
blurb: The system-sellers. Every one of these was built (or rebuilt) to prove a handheld could carry console-scale ambition, and most still define what people mean when they say 'PSP classic.'

games.title: God of War: Chains of Olympus
games.blurb: Kratos's PSP debut compresses full console-scale spectacle into a handheld, still cited as proof the format could do blockbuster action.

games.title: God of War: Ghost of Sparta
games.blurb: An even more ambitious sequel, widely considered the best-looking game ever squeezed onto PSP hardware.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker
games.blurb: A full mainline entry built for portable play, introducing the base-building and co-op systems that would later define Metal Gear Solid V.

games.title: Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories
games.blurb: The launch-window killer app that proved an open GTA city could fit in your pocket without losing the chaos.

games.title: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories
games.blurb: A sun-soaked prequel with a private-army subplot, widely regarded as Rockstar's most polished portable entry.

games.title: Patapon
games.blurb: Command a tribe of eyeball-warriors by drumming commands in rhythm — a genre unto itself and one of PSP's most original ideas.

games.title: LocoRoco
games.blurb: Tilt the whole world to roll a blob of singing jelly through hand-drawn levels; disarmingly simple and endlessly charming.

games.title: Lumines: Puzzle Fusion
games.blurb: Tetsuya Mizuguchi's block-matching puzzler synced to a pulsing electronic soundtrack — the launch title that defined what PSP could feel like.

games.title: Monster Hunter Freedom Unite
games.blurb: The game that made PSP a cultural phenomenon in Japan, built entirely around planning, hunting, and crafting gear with friends over ad-hoc Wi-Fi.

games.title: Wipeout Pure
games.blurb: Anti-gravity racing with a techno soundtrack and downloadable track packs, still one of the sharpest-looking racers the system ever produced.

games.title: Daxter
games.blurb: A spin-off starring Jak's wisecracking sidekick that plays like a full Jak & Daxter game in its own right.

games.title: Crisis Core: Final Fantasy VII
games.blurb: Zack Fair's tragic backstory to Final Fantasy VII, with real-time combat and a slot-machine-driven Limit Break system all its own.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts: Birth by Sleep
games.blurb: Three playable heroes and a decade of series lore packed into one of the best-reviewed action-RPGs on the system.

games.title: Persona 3 Portable
games.blurb: A leaner reworking of the PS2 classic that added a playable female protagonist and reshaped how the series would be remembered. Europe didn't get an official release, via Ghostlight, until nearly ten months after North America.

title: Tactics & Strategy RPGs
blurb: No platform's tactics shelf runs this deep. Grid-based war stories, bullet-hell strategy, and one entry the West never officially got to play.

games.title: Final Fantasy Tactics: The War of the Lions
games.blurb: A definitive remake of the PS1 classic with a sharper translation, new jobs, and anime cutscenes bridging the story's gaps.

games.title: Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together
games.blurb: Yasumi Matsuno's morally tangled war epic, rebuilt from the ground up with redrawn art and a reworked class system.

games.title: Jeanne d'Arc
games.blurb: A tactical RPG reimagining Joan of Arc's war as a fight against demonic invaders, praised for tight, generous mission design. Released in Japan and North America, but Europe never got a PSP release at all — a 2024 PS4/PS5 remaster was its first European release.

games.title: Valkyria Chronicles II
games.blurb: Trades the original's warfront for a military academy, keeping the series' hybrid of turn-based tactics and real-time movement intact.

games.title: Valkyria Chronicles III
games.blurb: The only mainline entry never localized in the West — Japan-only, following a disgraced penal unit through a story that's only been playable in English since a 2014 fan translation.

games.title: Disgaea: Afternoon of Darkness
games.blurb: Absurdly deep level-scaling and gag-heavy writing, the portable entry point to one of strategy-RPG's most obsessive fanbases.

games.title: Z.H.P.: Unlosing Ranger vs Darkdeath Evilman
games.blurb: A roguelike-tactics hybrid parodying sentai shows, as mechanically deep as it is deliberately ridiculous.

games.title: Knights in the Nightmare
games.blurb: A bullet-hell strategy RPG where you dodge enemy fire while directing an army of the dead — steep, strange, and like nothing else on the system.

games.title: Field Commander
games.blurb: A straightforward Advance Wars-style turn-based wargame, one of the few Western takes on the genre PSP received.

games.title: R-Type Tactics
games.blurb: The classic side-scrolling shoot-'em-up reimagined as grid strategy, with the series' bio-mechanical Bydo forces as the enemy army — released in North America under the title 'R-Type Command.'

title: JRPGs & Long Adventures
blurb: Between fresh remakes of PS1-era favorites and Falcom's action-RPG mainstays, this is where the PSP quietly became one of the best JRPG machines ever built.

games.title: Tales of Eternia
games.blurb: A PS1 favorite ported and polished — though its only Western release was in Europe; it never reached North America at all, one of the collection's rare EU-exclusive entries.

games.title: Ys: The Oath in Felghana
games.blurb: Fast, skill-based action-RPG combat that longtime fans still call the high point of the entire Ys series.

games.title: Ys Seven
games.blurb: The first mainline Ys built for a party system, trading solo swordplay for coordinated three-character combat across a much larger world.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky
games.blurb: A slow-burn, richly detailed fantasy epic that launched one of the most beloved long-running JRPG sagas in the West, though Europe had to wait about seven months longer than North America to get it.

games.title: Valkyrie Profile: Lenneth
games.blurb: A Norse-mythology RPG with platforming-based dungeon exploration and a battle system unlike anything else in the genre. Europe waited about nine months longer than North America for its release.

games.title: Star Ocean: Second Evolution
games.blurb: A remake of the PS1 fan favorite with a reworked battle system and an enormous private-action character web.

games.title: Lunar: Silver Star Harmony
games.blurb: A fresh remake of the beloved Sega CD classic, with new art, music, and a script rewritten for modern audiences.

games.title: Half-Minute Hero
games.blurb: A parody RPG where you must save the world in 30-second bursts before time resets, cramming an entire genre's tropes into bite-size missions.

games.title: Riviera: The Promised Land
games.blurb: A limited-inventory, side-scrolling RPG with a battle system built around weapon durability and split-second decisions. Its European release lagged North America's by about nine months.

games.title: Phantasy Star Portable
games.blurb: A single-player-friendly cut of the Phantasy Star Online formula, built for solo hunting between online sessions.

title: Action & Platformers
blurb: Console mascots shrunk down without losing their identity — plus a couple of oddballs, like a drill-wielding heroine, that never got the audience they deserved.

games.title: Ratchet & Clank: Size Matters
games.blurb: A console-quality entry in the series built from scratch for PSP, with new weapons and puzzle-driven Clank sequences.

games.title: Secret Agent Clank
games.blurb: A spy-themed spin-off putting Clank front and center, blending stealth, platforming, and gadget-based combat.

games.title: Castlevania: The Dracula X Chronicles
games.blurb: A gorgeous remake of Rondo of Blood that also unlocks the original PC Engine game and a port of Symphony of the Night.

games.title: Mega Man Powered Up
games.blurb: A chibi-styled remake of the original Mega Man with a level editor and extra playable Robot Masters.

games.title: Mega Man Maverick Hunter X
games.blurb: Mega Man X rebuilt in 2.5D with a new playable character route through Sigma's fortress.

games.title: Ultimate Ghosts 'n Goblins
games.blurb: A brutally difficult new entry in the series, softened only slightly by adjustable difficulty and RPG-lite gear upgrades.

games.title: LittleBigPlanet
games.blurb: A full-featured portable take on the create-and-share platformer, with a surprisingly deep level editor for a handheld.

games.title: Prinny: Can I Really Be the Hero?
games.blurb: A punishing side-scrolling spin-off of Disgaea starring an army of exploding penguin demons.

games.title: Gurumin: A Monstrous Adventure
games.blurb: A colorful action-RPG about a drill-wielding girl clearing monsters out of a mining town, warmly remembered as an overlooked Falcom gem.

title: Fighting Games
blurb: From arcade-perfect ports to a Final Fantasy crossover that became its own franchise, PSP's single analog nub turned out to be no obstacle at all.

games.title: Tekken: Dark Resurrection
games.blurb: An arcade-perfect Tekken running at a smooth framerate, long considered the best fighting game the system ever received.

games.title: Street Fighter Alpha 3 Max
games.blurb: The full 29-character Alpha 3 roster plus extras exclusive to this version, one of the most complete fighting-game packages on PSP.

games.title: Dissidia Final Fantasy
games.blurb: Final Fantasy heroes and villains across a dozen games clash in real-time arena battles wrapped in RPG progression systems.

games.title: Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy
games.blurb: A bigger, better-balanced sequel with a deeper roster and an actual explorable world map between fights.

games.title: Darkstalkers Chronicle: The Chaos Tower
games.blurb: A compilation of Capcom's gothic monster-fighter series with a new challenge tower mode layered on top.

games.title: SoulCalibur: Broken Destiny
games.blurb: Weapon-based 3D fighting brought to handheld with real depth, plus a guest appearance from Kratos of God of War.

games.title: Bleach: Heat the Soul 7
games.blurb: The final and most refined entry in the long-running Bleach fighter series, never localized outside Japan.

title: Shooters & Stealth Action
blurb: PSP quietly built a real third-person shooter identity of its own, anchored by Sony Bend's Syphon Filter games and console-caliber online multiplayer.

games.title: Syphon Filter: Dark Mirror
games.blurb: A stealth-action series returning to form on PSP, with mission design built specifically around handheld play sessions.

games.title: Syphon Filter: Logan's Shadow
games.blurb: A tighter, more cinematic sequel with expanded multiplayer and some of the best AI on the system.

games.title: Killzone: Liberation
games.blurb: Switches the console series' first-person view for isometric squad combat, and is often called PSP's best ad-hoc multiplayer shooter.

games.title: Resistance: Retribution
games.blurb: A console-caliber third-person shooter set during the Chimeran invasion of Europe, built exclusively for the handheld.

games.title: SOCOM U.S. Navy SEALs: Fireteam Bravo 2
games.blurb: Tactical squad shooting with a strong online component that made PSP a legitimate multiplayer FPS platform.

games.title: Metal Gear Acid 2
games.blurb: A turn-based, card-driven spin-off of Metal Gear that trades stealth action for tactical deck-building.

games.title: Coded Arms
games.blurb: A procedurally generated first-person shooter set inside cyberspace, one of the system's earliest attempts at an FPS built for its hardware.

games.title: Medal of Honor: Heroes 2
games.blurb: A WWII shooter with a surprisingly robust ad-hoc and infrastructure multiplayer suite for its time.

title: Racing & Speed
blurb: From Ridge Racer's launch-day drift handling to a kart racer with its own track editor, PSP's racing shelf lost surprisingly little in the trip from console to handheld.

games.title: Ridge Racer
games.blurb: A launch-day arcade racer with drift-heavy handling that showed off the PSP screen's colors from day one.

games.title: Burnout Legends
games.blurb: A greatest-hits compilation of the series' best tracks and crash modes, tuned specifically for shorter handheld sessions.

games.title: Midnight Club 3: Dub Edition
games.blurb: Open-city street racing with deep car customization, ported down from consoles without losing its personality.

games.title: MotorStorm: Arctic Edge
games.blurb: Off-road racing across icy terrain with genuinely dangerous environmental hazards like avalanches and cracking ice.

games.title: OutRun 2006: Coast 2 Coast
games.blurb: Breezy, arcade-perfect Ferrari racing across sun-drenched coastal routes, built for pure pick-up-and-play fun.

games.title: Split/Second
games.blurb: Racing where triggering environmental explosions can reroute the entire track mid-race, translated onto PSP without losing its spectacle.

games.title: Twisted Metal: Head-On
games.blurb: Vehicular combat mayhem that many longtime fans consider the true sequel the series deserved after its console entries stumbled.

games.title: ModNation Racers
games.blurb: Kart racing with a deep track and character creator, letting players build and share their own courses.

title: Puzzle, Party & Rhythm
blurb: PSP's short-session soul comes through clearest here — block-matching, drum-command armies, and a shoot-'em-up where the goal is to blow yourself up.

games.title: Lumines II
games.blurb: A sequel swapping in licensed pop and rock tracks, with a sequencer mode letting players remix the game's own music.

games.title: Patapon 2
games.blurb: Expands the original's rhythm-command formula with new unit types and a much bigger evolution tree for your tribe.

games.title: Patapon 3
games.blurb: A faster-paced, hero-focused entry closing out the trilogy with tighter drum-command combat.

games.title: LocoRoco 2
games.blurb: More tilting, more singing blobs, and trickier secrets layered onto an already-perfected formula.

games.title: Every Extend Extra
games.blurb: A chain-reaction shoot-'em-up-puzzle hybrid where dying in a big enough explosion is the actual goal.

games.title: Me & My Katamari
games.blurb: The roll-everything-into-a-ball series shrunk down for handheld play without losing its surreal, joyful chaos.

games.title: Rock Band Unplugged
games.blurb: A clever solo reinvention of the band-rhythm formula where you control all instruments by switching between them on the fly.

games.title: Space Invaders Extreme
games.blurb: A trance-and-techno remix of the arcade classic, layering chain reactions and power-ups onto its familiar alien grid.

title: Sports & Simulation
blurb: A smaller shelf than most genres here, but a varied one — skateboarding, boxing, high-seas piracy, and a full baseball season all fit in a UMD case.

games.title: Tony Hawk's Underground 2 Remix
games.blurb: Story-mode skateboarding chaos and classic THPS goals, tuned well for the handheld's shorter play sessions.

games.title: Fight Night Round 3
games.blurb: A boxing sim built around its Total Punch Control system, stripped of its HUD for a more immersive feel.

games.title: SSX On Tour
games.blurb: Arcade snowboarding with rock-star showmanship and guest cameo courses, ported down without losing its trick-chaining flow.

games.title: Sid Meier's Pirates!
games.blurb: Swashbuckling sim-adventure blending ship combat, treasure hunting, and empire-building into one endlessly replayable sandbox.

games.title: ATV Offroad Fury: Blazin' Trails
games.blurb: Off-road quad-bike racing across muddy, trick-friendly tracks, a launch-era favorite for the system's arcade-sports crowd.

games.title: MLB 08: The Show
games.blurb: A surprisingly deep baseball simulation that proved a full season-length sports sim could work on the go.

title: Horror & Visual Novels
blurb: PSP's UMD format turned out to be a perfect fit for slow-burn dread and heavy text — including the games that quietly started two of horror gaming's biggest cult franchises.

games.title: Silent Hill: Origins
games.blurb: A prequel exploring how Alessa's cult came to be, with a weapon-degradation system that keeps combat as unnerving as the fog.

games.title: Corpse Party
games.blurb: A remake of a cult PC-98 horror visual novel about students trapped in a cursed, blood-soaked school; grim, tense, and unusually personal.

games.title: The 3rd Birthday
games.blurb: A Parasite Eve spin-off blending body-swapping action-RPG combat with survival-horror atmosphere.

games.title: Manhunt 2
games.blurb: A censorship-magnet stealth-horror game about a man escaping an asylum by any brutal means necessary. Its UK release, after the BBFC's ban and forced re-edit, landed exactly one year after North America's — October 31st both years.

games.title: Obscure: The Aftermath
games.blurb: Co-op survival horror about student friends fighting spore-mutated monsters, a lesser-known but genuinely tense B-movie throwback.

games.title: Steins;Gate
games.blurb: A time-travel visual novel now considered one of the medium's best, though its PSP original never left Japan — English speakers first got the game in 2014 via a PC release, with PS3 and Vita versions following in 2015.

title: Cult Classics, Curios & Japan-Only Gems
blurb: This is where a 'best of' list earns the word explorer. A murder-mystery visual novel that became a phenomenon, a hand-drawn tactics game that never left Japan, a fishing-rod platformer with a cult following all its own.

games.title: Gods Eater Burst
games.blurb: A monster-hunting action-RPG with a faster, blade-swapping combat style that built its own passionate following alongside Monster Hunter.

games.title: Metal Slug XX
games.blurb: Run-and-gun arcade action with new vehicles and a boss rush mode, a pure shot of old-school SNK spectacle.

games.title: Taiko no Tatsujin Portable DX
games.blurb: Over 70 tracks of taiko-drumming rhythm action, Japan-only and never localized, but a favorite among import collectors.

games.title: Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc
games.blurb: The murder-mystery visual novel that launched a cult phenomenon, originally released only in Japan on PSP by developer Spike (which wouldn't merge into Spike Chunsoft until 2012), years before its 2014 English localization on Vita.

games.title: Fate/Extra
games.blurb: A tactical-action RPG spin on the Fate universe, localized against the odds and beloved by the franchise's Western fanbase — North America (Aksys Games, 2011) and Europe (Ghostlight, 2012) got it from two different publishers, about half a year apart.

games.title: Grand Knights History
games.blurb: A gorgeous, hand-drawn strategy-RPG hybrid from the Odin Sphere team, never released outside Japan — XSEED had an English translation essentially finished before cancelling the localization in 2012.

games.title: Nayuta no Kiseki
games.blurb: An open-area action-RPG in the Ys mold and one of the last major PSP RPGs Falcom ever made — Japan-only on PSP; English speakers had to wait until 2023's Switch/PS4/PC remaster, The Legend of Nayuta: Boundless Trails, to play it at all.

games.title: Tales of VS.
games.blurb: A Smash Bros.-style crossover brawler starring heroes from across the entire Tales series — never localized, Japan-only, played outside Japan almost exclusively via fan translation.

games.title: Class of Heroes
games.blurb: An old-school, grid-based first-person dungeon crawler that scratched a nostalgic itch for Wizardry-style RPG fans. Released in North America, but never in Europe.

games.title: Umihara Kawase Portable
games.blurb: A physics-driven platformer about swinging from a fishing line, cultishly adored for its elastic, momentum-based movement. Japan-only on PSP — a planned U.S. localization, Yumi's Odd Odyssey, was announced and then quietly cancelled.

title: Licensed, Ports & Movie Tie-Ins Done Right
blurb: Closing the collection with the genre most players write off entirely — proof that a licensed superhero or movie game could still hold its own on this handheld.

games.title: Star Wars: The Force Unleashed
games.blurb: A scaled-down but still spectacle-driven take on Starkiller's story, with lightsaber combat built around the handheld's controls.

games.title: Dante's Inferno
games.blurb: A God of War-inspired hack-and-slash through the nine circles of Hell, condensed without losing its over-the-top brutality.

games.title: X-Men Legends II: Rise of Apocalypse
games.blurb: Squad-based superhero action RPG with nearly two dozen playable mutants and drop-in co-op.

games.title: Marvel: Ultimate Alliance
games.blurb: A roster of Marvel heroes team up across a sprawling action-RPG campaign, console-scale ambition packed onto a UMD.
